name: US sales-tax license and registration lookup
demand: Exact search volume, installs, and the number of small sellers entering additional states are unverified. Useful proxies are 36,132 active registrations through the free Streamlined Sales Tax Registration System as of 2026-09-30 (not annual demand or total US registrations), and US retail e-commerce sales of $340.2B in Q2 2026 (market context, not a seller count). The SBA’s 36,207,130 small businesses are a broad ceiling based on 2022 data, not this product’s addressable market. Sources: https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/for-businesses/sales-tax-registration-sstrs/taxcloud ; https://www.census.gov/retail/eCommerce.html ; https://advocacy.sba.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/FINAL_FAQsAboutSmallBusiness_2026_012826.pdf
prices: Avalara lists License Guidance from $119 and sales-tax registration at $403 per location: https://www.avalara.com/us/en/products/pricing.html. TaxJar lists registration at $299 per state, for paid-plan customers: https://www.taxjar.com/product/registrations. LegalZoom lists business-license research and management at $99/year: https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/business-licenses-overview.html. Foundra advertises a free preview and a $19 one-off report, while its site still describes the service as a beta: https://www.foundra.us/. Registration itself can be free: SST registration has no system fee, and California’s online registration system is free to use, though a state may charge a fee or deposit: https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/for-businesses/sales-tax-registration-sstrs/taxcloud ; https://www.cdtfa.ca.gov/services/registration.htm
copy_speed: A close free adjacent product is listed by Mozilla as version 1.0.1, last updated 2026-10-08: it searches 78 US cities for general license rules, fees, renewal information, and official sources; the initial launch date is unverified, and it is not specifically a state sales-tax registration lookup. Source: https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/us-city-business-license-finde/. LegalZoom announced its AI business-license research product on 2026-03-25, before the requested 2026-04-23 cutoff; it describes a multi-agent system and claims a 40,000-license database and about 10,000 unique research requests per month, all vendor-reported: https://www.legalzoom.com/press-releases/legalzooms-ai-powered-business-license-platform. Foundra is a current $19 beta, but its launch date is unverified: https://www.foundra.us/. DC’s official BOSS licensing and registration platform launched 2026-08-10, but is a government alternative for DC rather than a national commercial competitor: https://dlcp.dc.gov/es/node/1841586. BizLicense advertises a November 2026 launch, so it is announced, not yet launched as of 2026-10-23; its coverage claims are vendor-reported: https://www.bizlicense.com/. No dated post-cutoff launch of an exact commercial state sales-tax registration lookup was verified in this search.
platform_risk: Medium-high: the product would sit beside free official state tools and free SST registration, while some sellers may not need a separate registration in particular situations; California, for example, says sellers using only a registered marketplace facilitator need not register as retailers with CDTFA. An SEO-only funnel would also depend on search rankings; a Shopify App Store funnel would depend on Shopify review and policies, which Shopify says can change. These channel-dependency ratings are assessments. Sources: https://www.sba.gov/counseling/launch-your-business/state-registration-lookup/ ; https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/for-businesses/sales-tax-registration-sstrs/taxcloud ; https://cdtfa.ca.gov/formspubs/pub51/getting-started-and-filing-your-return.htm ; https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/shopify-app-store/app-store-requirements
defensible_asset: A source-linked, maintained rules engine with dated changes would qualify as the required data moat if actually built and kept accurate. At launch, it is only a plan: public state information is reproducible, Avalara already publishes a state license directory, and LegalZoom sells license research, updates, and management while claiming broad jurisdiction coverage. There is no network effect, and a one-off lookup has little switching cost. LegalZoom’s database and automation figures are vendor claims, not independently verified. Sources: https://www.avalara.com/us/en/learn/licenses.html ; https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/business-licenses-overview.html ; https://www.legalzoom.com/press-releases/legalzooms-ai-powered-business-license-platform
build_effort: Moderate for a tightly scoped state-level sales-tax checklist and registration directory; very high if expanded into general state and local licensing. The SBA says requirements vary by business activity, location, and government rules; TaxJar says its experts research hundreds of regulations annually. Automated source extraction and change detection can help, but legal-quality review and source freshness remain material work. Independent build-hour and maintenance-hour estimates are unverified. Sources: https://www.sba.gov/counseling/launch-your-business/ ; https://support.taxjar.com/article/1227-frequently-asked-questions-taxjar-pricing-changes ; https://www.legalzoom.com/press-releases/legalzooms-ai-powered-business-license-platform
channel: Inbound SEO pages for state-specific registration questions, plus exact-intent paid search; later, a relevant Shopify or accounting integration marketplace listing and inbound partner referrals. No cold outreach is needed. UK marketing claims must be accurate and substantiated, and US ad claims must be truthful and evidence-based; Shopify App Store apps must follow its review and listing requirements. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/marketing-advertising-law ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/advertising-marketing ; https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/shopify-app-store/app-store-requirements
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; no operating product exists to measure. The ≤5h/week ceiling is not demonstrated, especially if human review is needed to keep legal requirements current.
automation_reason: Planning estimate for a narrow, state-only product: self-serve search, checklists, exports, billing, onboarding, routine support, and source-change alerts could be agent-run. Human review would still be needed for ambiguous legal changes and exceptions, so this does not establish that total workload stays under Ricardo’s time cap. LegalZoom describes AI completing a majority of its research requests but says some still require human review; that is a vendor-reported comparison, not evidence for this product. Sources: https://www.legalzoom.com/press-releases/legalzooms-ai-powered-business-license-platform ; https://support.taxjar.com/article/1227-frequently-asked-questions-taxjar-pricing-changes
moat_assessment: Conditional moat potential, not a current moat. A maintained, cited dataset with change history could satisfy the data/rules-engine requirement, but the broad version faces existing data-heavy incumbents and free government alternatives. Narrow the product to state sales-tax registration prerequisites and application steps, then make source dates and changes the core asset. Low switching costs mean paid exports alone are unlikely to create durable retention. Sources: https://www.avalara.com/us/en/learn/licenses.html ; https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/business-licenses-overview.html ; https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/for-businesses/sales-tax-registration-sstrs/taxcloud
desk_test: One-day smoke test: create three source-linked state registration checklists and a landing page offering a manually delivered $19 PDF, then run only exact-intent Google Search ads with a small fixed spend cap. Count a non-friend completed purchase as the signal; clicks and waitlist signups alone do not validate willingness to pay. Clearly identify the product as independent and substantiate every compliance claim. The $19 price matches Foundra’s advertised report price, not a proven market-clearing price. Sources: https://www.foundra.us/ ; https://support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/6020955?hl=en ; https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/advertising-marketing
red_flags: No verified product revenue, paid conversion, churn, or support burden was found; vendor list prices are not revenue proof. Exact target-market size and search demand are unverified. The paid service gap is narrower than the initial kill-check implied: LegalZoom sells license research and ongoing management for $99/year, Foundra advertises a $19 report, and free state/SST registration tools exist. Broad licensing scope creates substantial accuracy and maintenance work; TaxJar says its tax experts research hundreds of regulations annually. A report/export business also has weak repeat use unless customers pay for reliable change alerts. Sources: https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/business-licenses-overview.html ; https://www.foundra.us/ ; https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/for-businesses/sales-tax-registration-sstrs/taxcloud ; https://support.taxjar.com/article/1227-frequently-asked-questions-taxjar-pricing-changes
